result.summary: Revives a previously closed PR (#27837) that adds a BlockRequestTracker to net_processing so blocks manually requested via getblockfrompeer are automatically retried from another peer if the original request fails or the peer disconnects. It reworks FetchBlock to accept an optional peer id (meaning 'any peer') and a retry flag, adds the tracker class with pending/in-flight bookkeeping, and extends the getblockfrompeer RPC with new peer_id-optional and retry parameters plus functional test coverage.
result.problem: Users calling getblockfrompeer previously had no way to recover automatically when the chosen peer failed to deliver the block or disconnected, since block delivery is asynchronous and the RPC gave no failure notification. This PR lets the node keep trying other peers instead of leaving the user to notice failure and retry manually.

open_concerns: luke-jr: the peer_id-optional / retry=true default combination is confusing ('sounds like a default of true is being expressed via Optional::OMITTED rather than an explicit default'), and suggested clarifying the RPC help text or making it work without retry.
luke-jr: booleans should not be positional RPC parameters; should be named-only, e.g. via an options object.
optout21 (author) notes the final commit re-introduces behavior removed earlier in the commit series and says he wants to reorder commits to avoid that churn.

result.card: This PR revives closed PR #27837, adding a BlockRequestTracker so blocks requested via the getblockfrompeer RPC are automatically retried from other peers if the original peer fails or disconnects, instead of silently stalling. The problem is a real user-reported gap (issue #27652: getblockfrompeer lacks failure notification and any-peer support), but the change only affects the manual RPC path, not regular block sync. Reviewer luke-jr requested changes to the new RPC parameters (positional boolean, ambiguous default) and the author has only promised to address it, not yet done so. The PR needs a rebase, is marked dirty, and conflicts with three other open PRs touching the same block-fetch code, making review timing awkward. No dependency blocks it outright, but its final interface shape is still contested.
